title: Reacting thermals with heredity and selection (SIMDH): a label carried in each cap's own fluid breeds true through fission, a trait-blind mutation makes a new kind during the run, and the kind with 10% more heat yield rises from 0 to 0.76-0.93 of the caps on 6/6 seeds against 0.25-0.48 in the neutral twin that gets the same mutation draws
summary: world.py is the reacting-thermals world (20261027T0040-c49-reacting-thermals-claim, 20261027T0209-c49-thermals-flow-heredity) with every cap labelled a at t=200 (lab_mode 1) and a mutation every 25 t (mut_dt): one uniform draw picks a burning pixel and the labels a and b are swapped in a 6-px disk there; the draw never reads a label. The labels are advected with the flow, made only where the cap burns (autocatalytically, kl r a (1-a-b)) and decay elsewhere; the heat yield is Q (1 + eps (a - b)). heredity2.py (labkit segmentation and tracker on T at 1 t frames, seeds 0-5, T=1200): with eps -0.1 (b favoured) the mean share of b caps over t=400-1200 is 0.85/0.93/0.88/0.76/0.84/0.89, in the eps 0 twin (same seeds, same mutation draw sequence) 0.48/0.31/0.38/0.25/0.38/0.38 (share_b.png). Births by kind (daughters at persistent splits) b:a = 593:103 favoured vs 138:396 neutral. Daughters keep the parent's kind at 661/676 (favoured) and 524/534 (neutral) splits; of the kind changes of living caps (tracks >= 10 t), 152/160 and 166/182 fall within 12 px and 15 t of a logged mutation. labkit packs (seeds 0, 1): 69/59 persistent splits, generation 8/9 (favoured), 56/42, generation 8/5 (neutral); divmove.py: 23/33 and 17/22 dividing caps travel >= 3 sqrt(area) between their own birth and division.

claims.statement: In pack_sel (WORLD_P eps -0.1, lab_mode 1, mut_dt 25; seeds 0 and 1) and in heredity2.py runs of seeds 0-5, caps formed from a random hot field all start as kind a; trait-blind mutations create kind-b caps, which breed true through fission (daughters keep the parent's kind at 661/676 splits) and, because they burn 10% hotter per unit fuel, out-divide kind a (593 vs 103 births) and take 0.76-0.93 of the population, against 0.25-0.48 in the eps 0 twin with the same mutation draws. The dividing caps rise 3 or more sqrt(area) between their own birth and division (23/33, 17/22).
claims.track: seed 0 (pack_sel/seed0), labkit track 575: a kind-b cap (label share a/(a+b) 0.23 in the rendered fixed-scale label channels at every rendered frame of its life, kindtrack.py) born by a split at t=905 rises 11.9 sqrt(area) (7.4 long axes) and divides at t=1066 into tracks 709 and 710; 709 keeps kind b, rises 9.9 sqrt(area) and divides at t=1172 (divmove.json)

controls_run.H: pack_neutral/ (eps 0, same seeds and mutation draw sequence, seeds 0 1) and m_s*_e0.json (seeds 0-5): the identical-draw neutral twin; per-kind births, mutation-linked flips and off-kind daughters in m_s*_e*.json
controls_run.M: g=0 twin of the parent world: 20261027T0040-c49-reacting-thermals-claim/pack_g0 (0/11 dividing spots travel 3 lengths)

claims.bd_control: Not rerun for the labelled world; the parent world's g=0 twin loses M (c51's review 20261027T0230-c51-review-thermals confirms on seed 7).

limits: The fitness effect is written: the label scales the heat yield directly. The twin gets the same sequence of mutation draws, but each draw picks a burning pixel of its own state, so the mutated caps differ between arms after the first event (identical draw times and random numbers, not identical targets). Mutation is frequent (one per 25 t, ~39 per run) and symmetric, so the neutral twin drifts toward b as well (0.25-0.48); deaths by kind in the json count every track that ends without children, which includes tracker breaks of thin arcs, so only births are reliable per kind. The label share in kindtrack.py is read from labkit's fixed-scale rendered channels, so it shows the kind, not the true ratio. M is buoyant rise along gravity (see the parent claim); E is not claimed here. 128^2, T=1200, one parameter point; no dt/2 or resolution test of the labelled world.
